A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAM3C and RoomTours research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable, including discussion and limitations relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original semantic and instance segmentation experiments, component ablations, hyperparameter analyses, and a pre-training contamination comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains original segmentation and ablation results and adds a clean-versus-noisy pre-training comparison and cumulative component analysis.

M1.justification: The architecture, pipeline, and displayed objectives remain unchanged, and Huber regularization already appears in v1's appendix. However, v1 Appendix C describes penalizing deviation from the neighbor mean, whereas v2 describes pairwise edge differences and explicitly mentions degree normalization. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or its description was corrected.

E1.justification: Both retain the same RoomTours video sources and indoor semantic/instance segmentation coverage on ScanNet, ScanNet200, ScanNet++, and S3DIS. The new controls use existing datasets. Standardizing RoomTours-50k to RoomTours-49k does not change the documented 49,219-scene collection.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain PTv3, MSC, PPT, and the same Sonata variants; the reconstruction comparison retains VGGT, MapAnything, and pi3. New analyses reuse Sonata. Removed mixed-data LAM3C rows represent training configurations, rather than different comparison methods.

E3.justification: v2 adds the clean ScanNet versus RoomTours-1k control design and cumulative component settings, while removing mixed real-plus-video LAM3C configurations from Tables 1, 2, and 4. It also corrects limited-scene prose from 40% to the already-tabulated 20% and changes linear-probing backbone learning rates to N/A. These corrections do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 5 tests whether LAM3C's advantage depends on noisy reconstructed data rather than clean scans. New Figure 9 presents cumulative reconstruction, alignment, regularization, data-scaling, and model-scaling stages, partly reusing existing results. Earlier individual ablations, hyperparameter analyses, and contamination checks are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for the experimental scores. Point-estimate reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises RoomTours-49k/PTv3-Base ScanNet Full-FT mIoU from 75.1 to 77.7 and PTv3-Large ScanNet200 Full-FT from 35.5 to 35.9; Table 3e repeats the first update. Mixed real-plus-video result rows disappear from Tables 1, 2, and 4. Table 5 adds the clean-data LAM3C score of 66.8 versus Sonata's 67.1, and Figure 9 adds intermediate component scores. Most existing results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, Gaussian edge weights, and the scene-scale definition are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or removed. The corrected teacher/student index explanation does not change the displayed mathematics.

C1.justification: The conclusion newly specifies that the contribution concerns scalable, scan-free pre-training through video-only data collection rather than the input format itself. This modestly refines the contribution's scope; the central RoomTours, noise-regularization, and competitive segmentation claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of learning global context without hand-crafted indoor priors, interprets Table 5 as showing no inherent advantage on clean scans, and explicitly limits applicability in highly dynamic environments. It also revises the limited-supervision interpretation and drops the earlier domain-gap explanation. Dependence on reconstruction models trained with real point clouds was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code availability link and expands the documented regularizer implementation. It clarifies the default versus scaled training schedules and corrects the large-model footnote from 434k to 437k steps, consistent with the unchanged 436,800 iterations in both appendices. The Laplacian schedule wording is also corrected from decreasing to increasing.

R1.justification: v2 adds a formal Concerto reference for the large-backbone configuration, although v1 already named that work. The conclusion more explicitly positions the contribution around scalable video-derived pre-training data. The related-work survey and other cited works are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes the abbreviation VGPC, edits grammar and terminology, revises the conclusion, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. Discussion and limitations move from the main text to Appendices E and F. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5 and Figure 9, removes mixed-data rows from three tables, and adjusts highlighting and page flow. Figure 1 corrects the instance-segmentation axis to mAP and labels zero real scans; Figure 8's caption identifies pre-alignment point counts. Existing figure imagery and the overall layout are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The new clean-data control, code-access information, and documentation corrections improve interpretability. However, mixed-data evidence is removed while complementarity claims remain. New Figure 9 also reports 54.3 for aligned Sonata, versus 51.1 in Table 3c and Table 5, without sufficient settings information to reconcile them. These benefits and unresolved evidentiary drawbacks prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
